item.title: Achieving Heisenberg limit under noisy conditions with quantum Zeno dynamics and dynamical decoupling
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Kok Chuan Tan, Ke Zeng, Bakmou Lahcen, Jiang Yu
Quantum Zeno dynamics (QZD) and dynamical decoupling (DD) are useful tools that enable the effective suppression of noise in quantum systems. We consider the problem of when (i) noise can be suppressed and (ii) Heisenberg limit (HL) can be achieved in quantum metrology, and prove necessary and sufficient conditions for when QZD and DD are useful for achieving these two goals. We further show this condition can hold even when the Hamiltonian-not-in-Lindblad-span (HNLS) condition fails, allowing QZD/DD to recover Heisenberg scaling beyond what is certified by the usual HNLS-based quantum error correction (QEC) criterion. Finally, we demonstrate that the combination of both techniques can allow individually imperfect QZD and DD strategies to saturate HL.

item.title: Spin rephasing helps quantum memories store single-photon states longer for future networks
item.description:
📚 Physics News
We are continuously sending information to each other, transmitting zeros and ones through a giant network of connected computers and devices. Scientists are now trying to extend this familiar concept of the internet to the quantum realm, looking for an efficient way to exchange quantum rather than classical information: qubits instead of bits. The motivation is not just scientific curiosity. Qubits can be a 0, a 1 or any superposition of the two. They can also become entangled, showing a degree of correlation that is out of reach for classical bits.

item.title: Explainable artificial intelligence in interface design influences user outcomes and cybersecurity literacy
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Ahmed Al-sa'di, Mahmoud Al-Sarayreh, Esraa Ahmad
Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) exposes information that users can examine when assessing AI-generated recommendations. However, limited evidence is available on whether explanation-supported interaction develops competencies relevant to privacy and cybersecurity literacy. This study examined whether an XAI-enhanced design tool affects creative confidence, perceived learning, reported trust, perceived autonomy, and usability during a UI design task. We conducted a controlled between-groups experiment with 128 participants. Participants were randomly assigned to an XAI condition (n = 64) or a standard AI condition (n = 64). item.description:

👤 Princely Kolle Epie, ‪Gökhan Coşkun‬
